A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoAlign research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–C are readable, allowing reliable matching across revisions and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original molecular-property prediction, zero-shot molecule–morphology retrieval and hyperparameter experiments in Tables 2–4, Figure 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated baselines and target-removal ablations, including Table 5.

M1.justification: Both retain the context graph, degree-based random walks, GIN encoder, modality-specific MLP decoders and reconstruction-plus-Gaussian-KL objective. V3 rewrites the objective using probabilistic notation and negative log likelihood without establishing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The described context-graph sources, four prediction datasets and two retrieval datasets remain unchanged. Table 1 retains the same individual task and molecule counts. V3's inconsistent 685-task summary does not identify any added or removed tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add eight evaluated comparators: GraphCL, GROVER, JOAO, MGSSL, GraphLoG, GraphMAE, DSLA and UniMol. These extend the pretrained graph-model comparisons substantially, increasing the maximum baseline count from 19 to 27. Existing comparators, including the retrieval baselines, remain.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled pretraining settings that separately omit molecular, cell-morphology or gene-expression targets. These are new ablation settings; the original scaffold splits, AUC/MAE metrics, retrieval procedures and 80/196 retrieval-pair counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.3.1 and Table 5 add systematic target-removal ablations across all four prediction datasets, directly testing each modality's contribution. V1 lacks these component tests. The existing regularization-strength and walk-length sensitivities, plus appendix task-level analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations from ten runs. V3 extends that reporting style to additional results without introducing a different run count, seed-reporting practice, confidence interval or significance test.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive baseline and ablation results. Figure 3 changes Broad6K's structure-only task-win share from 62.5% to 90.6% with the expanded comparison pool. ChEMBL2K cell-morphology GP AUC changes from 51.5 to 50.1. Some high-AUC-threshold columns from v1's appendix disappear; the main InfoAlign scores and Table 4 retrieval results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 corrects the cumulative path-weight product for node i from edges indexed through i to edges indexed through i−1. The variational bounds, decoder-versus-InfoNCE proposition and Appendix A proof arguments otherwise retain their substance; most mathematical rewriting is notational.

C1.justification: The central methodological, theoretical and zero-shot claims remain. The introduction replaces the +10.58% Broad6K and +6.33% Biogen3K headline with improvements up to 6.4% against the expanded comparator pool. The abstract also broadens the explicit comparison claim from 19 to 27 baselines.

C2.justification: V3 revises the interpretation of structure-based methods toward the stronger performance of newer pretrained graph models. It also adds dataset-specific explanations of the target-removal ablations, including the greater importance of gene-expression targets on ChEMBL2K and ToxCast. Existing applicability discussion is largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds implementation-source attribution for GraphCL/GROVER/JOAO and RoBERTa/GPT2. Figures 6–7 now identify the predictors underlying their representation curves. Existing hardware, dataset-processing and context-graph construction disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting the expanded baselines and implementation provenance, including GraphMAE, DSLA, GraphLoG, JOAO, Uni-Mol and Datamol, while dropping the VAE and GCN references. The related-work narrative and positioning against CLOOME and InfoCORE remain largely intact.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the problem definition, node/edge/path descriptions and probabilistic encoder–decoder notation. Implementation becomes a separate Section 5, and RQ3 becomes a performance-analysis section containing ablations and hyperparameter analysis. Much of the introduction, related work and conclusion is retained.

P2.justification: V3 consolidates the compact main comparisons and v1's Appendix Tables 5–8 into expanded, category-grouped Tables 2–3, and adds a new ablation Table 5. Figures are relocated, Figures 1/2/5 are revised, and appendix captions expand. Figure 1 also corrects the contrastive modality blocks from decoders to encoders.

improvement.justification: The expanded graph-model comparisons and four-dataset modality ablations substantially address v1's empirical support gaps. Stronger baselines narrow the Broad6K advantage from about 10.6% to 4.0% while preserving it, making the comparative claim better tested. Lost high-threshold results and summary inaccuracies—685 tasks versus Table 1's 696, and a claimed minimum gain of 2.5% versus roughly 1.7% on ToxCast—are drawbacks, but do not outweigh the stronger evidence for comparative performance and modality contributions.
